_comment: Licence catalogue: texts in texts/<id>.txt (verbatim SPDX text, copyright placeholders templated; LicenseRef-* are our own and need legal review). Tags are described in advisor.json.

licenses.name: MIT License
licenses.summary: Do almost anything, keep my copyright notice, no warranty.
licenses.tradeoffs: Anyone can close-source your code and sell it. No patent grant.

licenses.name: BSD 2-Clause License
licenses.summary: Like MIT: keep my notice, no warranty.
licenses.tradeoffs: Same as MIT: no protection against closed forks.

licenses.name: BSD 3-Clause License
licenses.summary: Like MIT, and you cannot use my name to endorse your product.
licenses.tradeoffs: Same as MIT: no protection against closed forks.

licenses.name: ISC License
licenses.summary: MIT in fewer words.
licenses.tradeoffs: Same as MIT.

licenses.name: zlib License
licenses.summary: Do almost anything; do not claim you wrote it; mark changed versions.
licenses.tradeoffs: Same as MIT.

licenses.name: BSD Zero Clause License
licenses.summary: No conditions at all, no warranty.
licenses.tradeoffs: No credit required; no protection.

licenses.name: The Unlicense
licenses.summary: Public domain dedication for software.
licenses.tradeoffs: Public-domain dedication is shaky in some countries (CC0 or 0BSD are safer). No credit, no protection.

licenses.name: Apache License 2.0
licenses.summary: Permissive, with an explicit patent licence and patent-retaliation.
licenses.tradeoffs: Longer; notice and change statements required; not compatible with GPL-2.0-only.

licenses.name: Mozilla Public License 2.0
licenses.summary: Changes to my files must stay open; the rest of your product may stay closed.
licenses.tradeoffs: File-level copyleft; some companies avoid it.

licenses.name: GNU LGPL v3
licenses.summary: Library can be linked from closed programs; changes to the library stay open.
licenses.tradeoffs: Linking rules are hard to follow for apps that bundle code (JS, mobile).

licenses.name: GNU GPL v3
licenses.summary: Anyone who distributes it or a work built on it must share all source under GPL.
licenses.tradeoffs: Closed-source products cannot include it; running it as a hosted service does not trigger sharing.

licenses.name: GNU AGPL v3
licenses.summary: Like GPL, and also when others offer it over a network: they must share their source.
licenses.tradeoffs: Strongest open-source deterrent against closed SaaS clones; many companies refuse AGPL dependencies.

licenses.name: European Union Public Licence 1.2
licenses.summary: Strong copyleft written for EU law, in all EU languages, compatible with GPL, MPL and others.
licenses.tradeoffs: Copyleft covers network use as well; less known outside Europe.

licenses.name: Business Source License 1.1
licenses.summary: Source is open to read; production use is limited by terms you set; converts to an open licence on a change date (max 4 years).
licenses.tradeoffs: Not open source. You must fill in the parameters (grant, change date, change licence). Community tools may reject it.

licenses.name: Functional Source License 1.1, MIT future
licenses.summary: Anyone can use it for anything except a competing product; becomes MIT after 2 years.
licenses.tradeoffs: Not open source. Simple and tested; convert date is fixed at two years.

licenses.name: Functional Source License 1.1, Apache 2.0 future
licenses.summary: Same as FSL-MIT; becomes Apache-2.0 after 2 years.
licenses.tradeoffs: Not open source.

licenses.name: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0
licenses.summary: Free for non-commercial use only; commercial use needs a separate deal.
licenses.tradeoffs: Not open source. Stops commercial users, including your own competitors.

licenses.name: PolyForm Small Business 1.0.0
licenses.summary: Free for small organisations (under 100 people and about 1M USD revenue); bigger ones pay.
licenses.tradeoffs: Not open source. Revenue thresholds are fixed in the text.

licenses.name: Creative Commons Zero 1.0
licenses.summary: Public domain dedication for content and data, with a fallback licence.
licenses.tradeoffs: No credit, no protection; do not use for code with patents (use 0BSD or MIT).

licenses.name: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0
licenses.summary: Reuse freely, even commercially, if you credit me.
licenses.tradeoffs: Not meant for software. Anyone can reuse without sharing back.

licenses.name: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0
licenses.summary: Reuse freely if you credit me and share adaptations under the same licence.
licenses.tradeoffs: Copyleft for content; commercial users can still use it.

licenses.name: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0
licenses.summary: Reuse and adapt for non-commercial purposes only, with credit.
licenses.tradeoffs: Not open by OSI/DFSG definitions; the line between commercial and not is fuzzy.

licenses.name: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0
licenses.summary: Non-commercial reuse with credit; adaptations under the same licence.
licenses.tradeoffs: Same fuzzy NC line.

licenses.name: Creative Commons Attribution-NoDerivatives 4.0
licenses.summary: Share the work unchanged, even commercially, with credit.
licenses.tradeoffs: No remixes; not suitable if you want community contributions.

licenses.name: Proprietary Software Licence
licenses.summary: You may use the compiled software; no source, no copying, no resale, no hosting for others.
licenses.tradeoffs: Custom text: have counsel review before use. Enforceability varies by country.

licenses.name: Source-Available Licence (internal use, no competing use)
licenses.summary: Read it, run and modify it inside your organisation; do not redistribute or offer it as a competing product.
licenses.tradeoffs: Custom text: consider FSL or BUSL first (tested texts). Counsel review needed.

licenses.name: Assets Licence (all rights reserved)
licenses.summary: Art, audio and content may be seen and streamed as part of the product; not extracted, reused, or used for AI training.
licenses.tradeoffs: Custom text: counsel review needed.

licenses.name: All Rights Reserved notice
licenses.summary: No permission is granted to anyone.
licenses.tradeoffs: Use for private or unreleased work; it permits nothing. Not a replacement for a real licence if you ship.
